beats.text: The most charming person in the room? Might be a narcissist.
Students who had never met rated each other after short introductions.
The more narcissistic someone was, the more they were liked at first sight.
It was all surface: stylish clothes, confident body language, an entertaining way of talking.
But in another study, groups met again and again. By the seventh meeting, the narcissists' ratings had flipped. From likable to disliked.
So first impressions are easy to fake. Give it seven meetings.

sources: Back, Schmukle & Egloff (2010). Why are narcissists so charming at first sight? Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 98(1). 73 unacquainted freshmen, brief self-introductions; narcissism predicted popularity at zero acquaintance via clothing, confident body language, entertaining speech.

Paulhus (1998). Interpersonal and intrapsychic adaptiveness of trait self-enhancement. JPSP 74(5). Seven group meetings; narcissistic self-enhancers rated positively at first, negatively by the seventh. Via artfulparent summary.
